title: P1 — Evaluation of the Financial Reporting Framework
subtitle: Evaluating the Acceptability of the Financial Reporting Framework (FRF)
psrec_note: Apply the ISSAI 2210 hierarchy sequentially in Section 2. Then corroborate with the five-attribute assessment (Section 3). Conclude on engagement acceptability in Section 4.

sections.title: Identification & Context
sections.guidance: Identify the FRF being used, its purpose, and the legal basis (if any).

questions.text: Name of identified Financial Reporting Framework (FRF)
Purpose of the financial statements (General Purpose / Special Purpose)
questions.guidance: Per the IPSAS / IFRS Conceptual Framework.

questions.text: Based on the entity's nature / business model, is the identified FRF acceptable for the intended use of the FS?
questions.risk_description: FRF not appropriate to the entity's nature — pervasive risk to the entire engagement.
questions.inherent_risk_factor: Use of an FRF that does not fit the entity's business model produces statements that may not present a true and fair view.

questions.text: Is the FRF required by law or regulation?
questions.guidance: If Yes, Check A of the ISSAI 2210 hierarchy is satisfied and the FRF is presumed acceptable.

questions.text: Legal / regulatory source of the FRF mandate (if any)
questions.guidance: e.g. NBAA Technical Pronouncement No. 1 of 2018; Public Finance Act, Cap 348.

sections.title: ISSAI 2210 Hierarchy
sections.guidance: Apply sequentially. Stop at the first check that is satisfied.

questions.text: A. Is the FRF prescribed by law or regulation for general-purpose financial statements?
questions.guidance: If Yes → FRF is presumed ACCEPTABLE. The hierarchy stops here.

questions.text: B. Is the FRF set by an authorised or recognised standard-setting organisation?
questions.guidance: Only assess if Check A is No.

questions.text: C. If neither A nor B, is the framework constructed by management/TCWG on a justifiable basis?
questions.guidance: Only assess if A and B are both No.
questions.risk_description: FRF fails all three ISSAI 2210 hierarchy checks — engagement should not be accepted without modification.
questions.inherent_risk_factor: When none of the hierarchy checks are met, the FRF cannot be presumed acceptable and the auditor must consider declining the engagement.

sections.title: Five Attributes Assessment
sections.guidance: Even where the FRF is presumed acceptable under Check A, corroborate against the five qualitative attributes. Any 'No' triggers further consideration.

questions.text: Relevance — Does the information relate to the nature of the entity and the purpose of the FS?
questions.inherent_risk_factor: FRF does not produce information relevant to users — affects engagement acceptability.

questions.text: Completeness — Does the FRF cover all material transactions, events, balances and disclosures?
questions.inherent_risk_factor: Material gaps in the FRF leave classes of transactions or disclosures unaddressed.

questions.text: Reliability (i) — Does the information reflect the economic substance of events and transactions?
questions.risk_description: FRF attribute failure — Reliability (substance over form).
questions.inherent_risk_factor: The FRF does not require substance-over-form representation, undermining reliability.

questions.text: Reliability (ii) — Does the framework allow reasonably consistent evaluation, measurement, presentation and disclosure?
questions.inherent_risk_factor: Inconsistent recognition or measurement bases impair comparability and reliability.

questions.text: Neutrality — Is the information free from bias?
questions.inherent_risk_factor: The FRF does not enforce neutrality, potentially permitting biased recognition or presentation.

questions.text: Understandability — Is the information clear, comprehensive, and not subject to significantly different interpretations?
questions.inherent_risk_factor: Ambiguous or inaccessible disclosures permit divergent interpretations by users.

triggers.risk_description: Financial reporting framework is not acceptable — engagement should not be accepted without modification.
triggers.inherent_risk_factor: An unacceptable FRF undermines the basis for the auditor's opinion. The engagement should be declined or accepted only with a modified report.

options: ACCEPTS subject to communication of modification
DOES NOT ACCEPT the audit engagement

questions.text: Reason (if Not Acceptable, or if accepted with reservation)
questions.guidance: Required when S4_Q1 is anything other than 'Acceptable'.
